I purchased the 5.1 Cubic Foot Chest Freezer for a great price. I was so excited to get it today! We've been playing Tetris in our regular freezer for a long time. I was worried about buying a stand alone freezer because of space and energy consumption.

First, the freezer arrived in perfect condition (as far as I know so far). I was really worried because of some of the reviews. The packaging isn't ultra protective, so I will say that how it arrives probably has a lot to do on how poorly it is treated by the shipping carrier. Mine arrived fine through UPS.

It looks like the size is going to be about perfect for my husband and I. It will allow us to really stock up on frozen goods without it taking up too much room itself. The most standardized thing I can compare it to is that it is about the size of a dishwasher, but about five inches longer in the front. We have room for it in our kitchen/dining room area. It is of moderate size, but by no means as big as most standard chest freezers. If you have a really small space this might be a bit too big.

The lid to the freezer is light and it opens up very smoothly. Even someone with limited strength should have no issue lifting the lid. The freezer itself is not super heavy. I was able to set it up myself by carefully sliding the box into position. The box itself slides up and off the freezer. You can "walk" the freezer carefully off the Styrofoam base. The manual indicated to NEVER TILT IT

I purchased the original washing wand made with a wooden screw-in handle and separate 2-part rubber bottom. It was ok WITH issues. THIS version of the same type device is a SIGNIFICANT improvement that makes using it a PLEASURE! (Since when can doing hand washables be a pleasure??? LOL) Read on and I'll tell you...

The first breathing hand-powered washing device I bought was made w/ a wooden handle that did NOT screw securely into the base. One has to continually screw it back in during EACH use yet it STILL wiggles its way out of the base, all the while clicking annoyingly w/every up & down motion during use. That was my chief complaint along with it being a bit uncomfortable to hold onto as water does splash on the handle causing it to get slippery. BUT, since there was no comparable alternative I continued to use it for my infrequent hand washable loads. Then! Enter the EasyGo Hand Powered Clothes Washing & ALL the issues mentioned above went KAPUT!

It has a BIGGER base which is better designed for movement of water AS WELL AS a functional design for LEFT to RIGHT motion as well as UP & DOWN motion actually mimicking an electric washing machine as well as the HANDLE at the top that allows one to securely GRIP the device easily facilitating left to right motion without it slipping out of your hand. The cleverly placed vent holes at the top prevents a vacuum from forming as the water is forced through.

I like functional work-outs and by recog

Also, it is quite big when assembled and assembly is not as quick as to disassemble after every use.

All in all, ok but overpriced.

Using it to clean/agitate clothing requires minimal time and effort (my toddler even likes to take a crack at it!) and I'm glad I bought this.  While I would not recommend this as a substitute for a washing machine, it is perfect for those things that just need a good soak and rinse.

this my 4th set of reusable K-cups  My 1st set required hacking to work.  The next sets took 3 times too long to brew a cup of coffee.  Finally I found a K-Cup that the Keurig recognizes and brews almost as quick as Keurig disposable brand.
They work fine. The cleanup is a bit of a pain but worth it so far. I gave it three stars because I can already see the lid showing extreme wear after only ten uses.

Not sure why people have been leaving 5 star reviews, they obviously don't know what quality reusable K-cups look like. These work, but are messy, they are flimsy, and don't think they will last that long. The bottom of the cup is recessed so it doesn't have to be centered with the needle, however because of this it doesn't flow in a directed stream like others i've had and makes more of a splash getting water on the counter. They work and are cheap, but honestly, for a few dollars more you can get a better quality reusable k-cup.
